discovery: Discovery of the fractional quantum anomalous Hall effect: fractionally quantized Hall states at zero magnetic field in moire and rhombohedral graphene/TMD Chern bands

nominees.name: Long Ju
nominees.affiliation: Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Cambridge, USA

subfield: Condensed matter physics (topological phases, fractional quantum Hall physics)
motivation: For decades, fractionalized quantum Hall fluids were thought to require a strong magnetic field and Landau levels. Theory suggested that topology of Bloch bands alone should suffice, but whether nature would realize a fractional Chern insulator was an open question. In 2023-2024 Xu (twisted MoTe2, with optical and transport evidence), Mak (with Shan, in the same system) and Ju (rhombohedral pentalayer graphene on hBN) independently observed fractionally quantized Hall resistance at zero applied field, arising from spontaneous time-reversal breaking in flat topological bands. This shows that emergent anyonic topological order can come purely from electron correlations in a lattice band, with no Landau levels. It is conceptually profound, was confirmed quickly across laboratories and materials, and opens a new platform for studying non-Abelian states and anyons at zero field. It is a clear example of quantum mechanics being richer than we expected.
